messages:
zoe: Urgent — multiple customers hitting 429s and timeouts since ~09:12 UTC. Support ticket P-8935. Happening across hosted region eu-west-1.

support-bot: Alert: High 429 rate from limiter-service (hosted-prod). 09:14 UTC. Affected customers: 3 (acct-12, acct-77, acct-98).

dan: Any recent deploys to limiter? I can look at logs.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout limiter-service@v3.5.1 started 08:55 UTC, completed 09:05 UTC.

maria: I'm seeing limiter pods OOM or restart loops? Logs show repeated 'rate_limit_evict: global_burst_quota became negative' then 500s. Suspect burst pool arithmetic bug.

suresh: Hmm. There's an earlier PR that refactored refill rates (PR #712). It changed refill unit semantics but maybe not all callers. Could be using ms vs sec.

anya: Poking metrics — global_burst_pool_size spikes to 2.1e9 then drops to -1. Looks like integer overflow/underflow.

maria: Repro locally: hitting endpoint with a 1000 concurrent short requests reproduces 429s reliably. curl script:

``
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
``

maria: Limiter log snippet:

``
2026-03-15T09:13:21Z limiter[pid=23]: acquire: want=10, have=2147483647, pool=-2147483648
2026-03-15T09:13:21Z limiter[pid=23]: error: global_burst_quota negative, evicting
``

dan: That looks like 32-bit signed int overflow.

suresh: Confirmed in PR: refill calculation multiplied tokens/sec by 1000 but stored in int32. On high bursts it overflows. Bug introduced in limiter/refill.go lines 42-58.

maria: Mitigation options: 1) rollback limiter-service to v3.5.0 (safe), 2) hotfix patch changing types to int64 and clamp values, 3) temporary global quota cap.

zoe: Support asks for immediate action, customers are severely rate limited. I'll recommend rollback + quota cap till we patch.

dan: I'm initiating rollback now.

deploy-bot: Rollback triggered: limiter-service -> v3.5.0. Start 09:18 UTC.

maria: Also applying temporary kube patch to set env GLOBAL_BURST_CAP=50000 on limiter deployment to clamp bursts.

anya: Rolling restart limiter pods to pick up cap. 09:21 UTC.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers: email drafted. ETA for fix?

suresh: Working on hotfix branch. Patch changes refill math and uses int64. Quick diff:

``
- rate := int32(refillPerSec * 1000)
+ rate := int64(math.Round(refillPerSec * 1000))
+ if rate > maxRate { rate = maxRate }
``

suresh: Running unit tests + integration.

dan: Rollback complete; 429s dropped to baseline in ~2 mins according to metrics. 09:22 UTC.

maria: Verified customer traffic now passes. Support confirms reduced errors.

zoe: Great. Next steps: hotfix release + one-hour maintenance window to deploy v3.5.1-hotfix in canary then prod. Add integration test for high-burst scenario.

suresh: Agreed. I'll open PR with tests and request review from @maria and @dan.

anya: Also adding alert for large positive pool_size spikes and a guard that caps stored values to int64 limits.

zoe: Post-incident: we need a short incident note for docs, timeline + root cause + customer impact. I can draft.

maria: Adding follow-ups: 1) Code audit for other int32 uses, 2) Add CI smoke test for 1k concurrent calls, 3) Update runbook to include GLOBAL_BURST_CAP knob.

support-bot: Incident update: mitigated 09:22 UTC; rollback + cap applied; customers notified.

zoe: Thanks everyone. Filing postmortem and retro. :thumbsup: :spiral_note_pad:

suresh: PR #789 (hotfix) opened, requesting quick merge.

dan: I'll watch the deploy. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Canary hotfix deploy started 09:45 UTC.

deploy-bot: Hotfix canary passed health checks 09:48 UTC. Rolling to prod 09:50 UTC.

maria: Hotfix prod deploy successful 09:51 UTC. Monitoring closely.

support-bot: All affected customers acknowledged fix. Closing incident after postmortem.

zoe: Marking thread resolved. Thanks team. :party_parrot:
